transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2025-11-12 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), John Park (CTO, LumenHealth), Maya Singh (ML Engineer), Kevin O'Neil (PM)

Summary:
Redwood walked through the Eval / Quality Monitoring product (Console + API + Optimize recommendations). Focus: how LumenHealth can use prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons to monitor production drift and prevent quality regressions during model rollouts. Customer asked about privacy, SOC2, KMS, and integration with their existing CI/eval pipelines. Agreed next steps: security docs, eval templates, and POC scoping call.

Topics:
- Prompt sets and golden outputs
- Regression alerts and thresholds
- A/B comparisons / rollouts and metrics
- Console demo: prompt set UI, diffs, alerting rules, webhooks
- API and SDK examples for eval automation
- Security / SOC2 / KMS / data residency

Transcript:
00:00 Samantha Lee: hey everyone thanks for making time today, we'll run about 45 to 60 minutes, um quick agenda, i'll do a 10 minute overview and diego will demo the console and the eval flow, then q and a, cool?
00:12 John Park: sounds good, thanks Sam. quick note, our timeline for a POC is end of November, and we want to validate regressions when we move from gpt-3.9 to gpt-4-like open model variants, and also we need SOC2 docs because we're healthcare.
00:28 Samantha Lee: totally, that's what we'll cover - security, and the eval tools are built for exactly that, to catch regressions before they hit prod.
00:34 Diego Martinez: hey all, i'll share my screen in a sec - i'll start with the prompt set concept. so prompt sets are collections of real user prompts or synthetic cases you care about, you attach golden outputs (or expected labels) and then we run them against model versions to compute metrics.
00:52 Maya Singh: do you support fuzzy matching, like we don't always have exact golden text? we care about semantic similarity and also some custom pass/fail heuristics.
01:03 Diego Martinez: yes, you can define multiple metrics - exact match, ROUGE-style, embedding-similarity thresholds (we use cosine on embeddings), and custom JS scoring functions in the Console that run per-case. occasionally the transcriber acts up: i said "JS scoring" and it shows up as j s scoring in notes.
01:18 Kevin O'Neil: and for A/B, can you run a canary with 10% traffic and automatically alert if latency or quality drops?
01:26 Samantha Lee: yep, you can configure A/B buckets in the rollout; Redwood Optimize will surface cost/latency tradeoffs and the eval system can gate a rollout based on quality deltas you define.
01:36 Diego Martinez: (screen) okay here's the prompt-sets page - we've got a "clinical triage" set that contains 120 prompts, each with expected categories and golden text. you can import from CSV, paste, or hook to a repo. notice the tagging and metadata, you can filter by scenario, intent, or priority.
02:05 John Park: how do you handle PII? we can't send raw PHI to hosted endpoints without the right controls.
02:12 Samantha Lee: we have a private deployment option, VPC connectors, and you can encrypt at rest with customer-managed KMS. for hosted, we offer SOC2 and encryption in transit + at rest, and we can discuss a dedicated tenancy for the POC. i'll send the SOC2 and KMS notes after the call.
02:34 Maya Singh: good. on the eval metrics, can we do multi-turn evaluation and context carryover checks? a lot of our prompts rely on previous messages.
02:44 Diego Martinez: yes, the eval runner can accept conversation turns and you can store the whole session as a test case including KV-cache warm state. small caveat: when we run many multi-turn cases the runtimes increase - the Console surfaces projected cost per run.
03:05 Kevin O'Neil: can you show regression alerts?
03:10 Diego Martinez: sure - so here's the regression alerts UI. you set a baseline run (say model-v1 on date X) and then create alert rules: metric, threshold, window (like 5% drop in accuracy across last 100 samples), and notification targets (Slack, PagerDuty, or webhook). we'll demo an intentional regression.
03:33 Diego Martinez: running now - baseline metrics: accuracy 92%, embedding-sim 0.86 average. switching to model-v2 (test) - oh, look, accuracy dropped to 85% on the clinical triage set. alert fired, here are the diffs - you can see per-case highlights where the label changed.
03:53 Maya Singh: the per-case diff view is great. can we attach comments or link back to a ticket?
03:58 Diego Martinez: yep, you can create a ticket directly from the case and it links to your Jira or linear via integration. also comment threads for collaborators.
04:10 John Park: our big concern is false positives - we can't be flooded with alerts. how do you tune sensitivity without missing regressions?
04:20 Samantha Lee: you start with conservative thresholds and use evaluation windows + statistical significance checks; Redwood supports smoothing and requires sustained deltas over multiple windows before firing critical alerts. also alert severity levels let you route to different teams.
04:36 Diego Martinez: add to that, we support debouncing and grouping, e.g., if 30 cases fail but share the same root prompt we cluster them to one incident.
04:48 Kevin O'Neil: what's the integration path with our CI? we want to run evals on every PR or model push.
04:56 Diego Martinez: we have an API endpoint and an SDK - you can upload prompt sets and trigger runs. common pattern: run a smoke eval in CI on merged PRs, run full eval periodically, and trigger a canary rollout only if quality metrics pass. we also provide webhooks for run-complete events to feed back into your pipeline.
05:18 Maya Singh: do you have examples for healthcare-specific scoring? like we sometimes need redaction accuracy and intent classification metrics.
05:25 Diego Martinez: yes we have templates. for redaction we compute precision/recall on detected PHI spans and provide a visualization of span-level mismatches.
05:36 Samantha Lee: i want to call out the Optimize recommendations - after running evals, Redwood will suggest quantization or model variant swaps if cost increases without quality gains, and show token/unit cost impact.
05:50 John Park: does quantization ever change the outputs enough to trigger false regressions?
05:55 Diego Martinez: possibly; we recommend including quantized variants in the eval matrix. the Console treats them as distinct model versions so you can compare side-by-side.
06:07 Samantha Lee: quick note, sometimes the transcript picks up "quantization" as "congrats Asian" - ignore that.
06:15 (laughter)
06:20 Diego Martinez: demo continued - A/B comparisons: you can specify bucketing rules, traffic weights, and metric targets. the UI shows live rollup for latency, cost, and quality. you can also define gating rules so the system automatically halts a rollout if quality drops beyond your threshold.
06:44 Kevin O'Neil: what's the minimum sample size you need before making decisions? we have low traffic on some endpoints.
06:52 Diego Martinez: depends on metric variance; Console will surface recommended sample size and an estimated time to detect a delta at X confidence. if traffic is low we recommend synthetic prompt injections or running dedicated evaluation jobs.
07:08 Maya Singh: can we run offline batch evals against labeled holds so we don't touch prod?
07:14 Diego Martinez: absolutely - you can run runner jobs against datasets stored in S3 or internal repos, or run entirely in private deployment. the runner supports parallelization to speed up throughput.
07:28 John Park: on the alerting side, do you provide per-route token breakdowns so we can see cost impact of an A/B?
07:35 Samantha Lee: yes, cost dashboard by route/model and token-level breakdown is in Console Insights. it helps you attribute unit cost to flows and to see where optimizations pay off.
07:48 Kevin O'Neil: you mentioned webhooks - can we push regression events to our internal incident system with payload containing failing cases?
07:56 Diego Martinez: yes, webhook payload includes case id, prompt, golden, model output, metric deltas - PII can be redacted if you opt in.
08:12 Maya Singh: what's the data retention window for eval data? we have policy constraints.
:08:18 Samantha Lee: configurable - default 90 days for hosted, but Dedicated / Private can set policies per contract. we can also provide export hooks to your storage for retention alignment.
08:31 John Park: do you support thresholding on semantic similarity (embedding) and also allow a custom embedding model?
08:37 Diego Martinez: you can choose Redwood embeddings or bring-your-own via API key; thresholds are configurable per prompt-case and per prompt-set.
08:48 Maya Singh: for our POC, we want a regression alert if triage category accuracy drops >4% over a rolling 24h with significance. also notify ML team Slack channel and open a JIRA.
08:59 Samantha Lee: noted - that can be configured. we'll include it in the POC scoping doc.
09:05 Diego Martinez: now showing the case diff viewer - left is baseline output, right is candidate output, color-coded highlights where tokens changed, and an automatic severity estimate. the system attempts to cluster root-cause by template mismatch. sometimes the transcription note will show 'cluster rout cause' instead of root cause.
09:35 Kevin O'Neil: can the system do A/B statistical tests, like chi-square or bootstrap significance?
09:42 Diego Martinez: yes. we provide basic tests and also bootstrap confidence intervals; results are shown inline and you can export the raw numbers.
09:55 Maya Singh: okay for the POC, we'll need: (1) your runner integrated into our CI to run nightly evals on the clinical triage prompt set; (2) regression alerts to Slack + JIRA; (3) a canary gating rule on new model deploys.
10:10 Samantha Lee: perfect - we'll draft the POC responsibilities and acceptance criteria in the follow-up.
10:16 John Park: question on cost - how much compute do evals run typically consume? we have budget constraints.
10:24 Diego Martinez: depends on model size and number of cases; Console will estimate cost per run. for 120-case multi-turn sets on a 13B model it might be a few dollars per run; we'll share an estimate sheet. the Optimize tool will recommend smaller model variants or quantized builds if cost is high with similar quality.
10:46 Maya Singh: do you have any existing healthcare customers we can reference?
10:50 Samantha Lee: yes, we have a few and we can provide references under an NDA - i'll follow up.
10:58 Diego Martinez: moving to the API demo - here's the eval-run endpoint example, payload with prompt-set id, model version, and run parameters. common gotcha: make sure you pass the conversation context for multi-turn. the SDK has helpers to chunk and map outputs back to cases.
11:22 Kevin O'Neil: does the run API support streaming so we can see partial outputs?
11:27 Diego Martinez: for evals we usually run batch jobs; streaming is available for live endpoints but not typical for offline runner jobs.
11:36 Maya Singh: can we persist the KV cache and warm sequences between runs? some of our cases require warm state to trigger subtle behaviors.
11:44 Diego Martinez: yes you can store and replay KV cache snapshots - Console integrates that as an advanced option.
11:52 John Park: on security - are logs encrypted and do you provide audit logs for eval runs?
11:58 Samantha Lee: yes, audit logs are available, and logs are encrypted in transit and at rest. Dedicated/Private customers can bring their own KMS for key management.
12:10 Maya Singh: does Redwood store the raw model outputs by default? we might want only aggregated metrics stored.
12:17 Samantha Lee: you can opt out of storing full outputs or redact them; we also support exporting raw outputs to your S3 so Redwood doesn't retain them.
12:28 Diego Martinez: demo - creating an alert rule now and setting a 4% drop threshold, rolling window 24 hours, min samples 100, notifications to slack channel #ml-regressions and webhook to JIRA.
12:45 Kevin O'Neil: we're a bit worried about noisy cases; can you exclude low-confidence cases or weight cases by priority?
12:52 Diego Martinez: yes, cases have priority and weight; you can exclude or downweight low-confidence model outputs.
13:00 Maya Singh: how do you surface long-term trends vs short-term blips?
13:06 Diego Martinez: the Insights view has trend lines, seasonal decompositions, and anomaly detection over longer windows; you can create rolling baseline snapshots for comparison.
13:18 Samantha Lee: we should also talk about governance: RBAC for who can change alert rules or approve rollouts, SSO via SAML, and audit trails.
13:26 John Park: yes SSO and RBAC are must-haves.
13:30 Samantha Lee: fully supported.
13:33 Diego Martinez: quick note on noisy transcriptions - sometimes the export has names spelled oddly; ignore those.
13:40 (brief cross talk)
13:45 Diego Martinez: showing export options - CSVs, JSONL with per-case metadata, or parquet to S3 for large runs.
13:55 Maya Singh: we'll want the JSONL format to ingest into our internal dashboards.
14:00 Diego Martinez: ok, here's an example workflow for your POC: (1) import clinical-triage prompt set; (2) configure baseline runs against current prod model; (3) configure regression thresholds and Slack + JIRA alerts; (4) integrate runner into CI for nightly smoke runs; (5) run small scale canary with 10% traffic and gating rules.
14:26 John Park: timeline: we'd like to kick off next week with Redwood installing a trial instance or giving us tenancy - what's typical?
14:34 Samantha Lee: for hosted evals we can provision you a trial account within 2 business days; for Dedicated it's a bit longer - we'll scope it in the POC doc.
14:44 Kevin O'Neil: cost for trial?
14:47 Samantha Lee: trial credits cover baseline evals; we'll include pricing options in the follow-up.
14:52 Maya Singh: any gotchas we should watch for?
14:56 Diego Martinez: watch for prompt canonicalization differences - small punctuation or whitespace changes can look like regressions; include semantic metrics and set reasonable thresholds. also include unit tests for critical prompts in your CI.
15:10 John Park: ok let's recap and next steps.
15:13 Samantha Lee: recap: we'll send SOC2 + security notes, a POC scoping doc with responsibilities + acceptance criteria, eval templates and runner examples, and we'll schedule the POC scoping follow-up for 2025-11-19. action items we've noted.
15:31 Kevin O'Neil: thanks everyone, this was super helpful.
15:33 Maya Singh: thanks.
15:36 Samantha Lee: thanks all, we'll follow up via email.

End of transcript. Note: transcription includes occasional mis-typed words and name spellings per Fireflies style.
